_comment: Configuration for the 'event-modeling-agents-watch' scheduled task. Edit this file to change what the weekly watch looks for. The task reads it at the start of every run. Add/remove items freely; keep it valid JSON.
_scope_options: Each watch axis has its own scope. 'focus-only' = capture only items touching the listed topics (a narrow net for on-target material). 'anything-substantive' = capture any notable new post regardless of topic, flagging off-thread items in the report (used for the people watch, where the value is the author, not the keyword match). PER-TOPIC OVERRIDE: a topic may carry its own `scope` field, which TAKES PRECEDENCE over the global `topic_scope` for that topic. This lets the tight EM×agents intersection stay 'focus-only' while the broader design-substrate topics run 'anything-substantive'.
_social_topic_search: TOPIC-LEVEL SOCIAL SEARCH (added per Dannie 2026-07-08). In addition to the web `queries`, each topic may carry a `social_queries` object with `x` and `linkedin` term/hashtag lists. During a sweep, run these as keyword/hashtag searches ON the platform (X search + LinkedIn search), NOT as web searches — they surface topic discourse that never reaches a blog (the loop-engineering thread in particular lives on X first). A social hit inherits that topic's `scope` (focus-only topics keep only genuinely on-topic items; anything-substantive topics keep any notable hit and flag off-thread). This is DISTINCT from the people watch, which follows named authors; here the axis is the KEYWORD, so it catches new voices. CONSTRAINT: X/LinkedIn are login-walled + client-rendered, so these run ONLY in a LIVE logged-in Chrome session (Dannie is logged in) — navigate to the platform search URL, scroll, and collect post text+timestamps via javascript_tool (get_page_text alone returns too little); see `_x_coverage`. In a HEADLESS scheduled run, SKIP social_queries and note in the report that a live-Chrome sweep is needed to cover them (a plain web search for the same terms is a weak fallback, fine to run opportunistically). Dedupe social hits against raw/ and the people-watch finds so an author's post isn't filed twice. Social posts capture to raw/notes/.
_x_coverage: X/Twitter IS part of the people watch (STEP 2 says check each person's blog/linkedin/X). Like LinkedIn, X timelines are login-walled + client-rendered: headless WebFetch returns an empty shell and get_page_text grabs only the pinned tweet, so X posts otherwise enter the wiki only via incidental web-search hits. For a real X sweep, drive it in a LIVE logged-in Chrome session (Dannie is logged in): navigate to https://x.com/<handle>, then scroll + collect article text/timestamps via javascript_tool (get_page_text alone only returns the pinned tweet). Added per Dannie 2026-06-19. Per-person `x` handles are listed below; treat them with the same anything-substantive + flag-off-thread rule as LinkedIn. Observed 2026-06-19: adymitruk = off-thread World Cup reposts; vladikk = short AI-economy aphorisms (substance stays on his blog) — both quiet on-thread.

_linkedin_live_sweep_mechanics:
ADDED 2026-09-04 from the first real live-Chrome social sweep. Four things the config previously assumed wrongly:
(1) FEED DEPTH IS CAPPED AT ~5 POSTS per recent-activity page in this extraction path. The 'Show more results' button on those pages belongs to the SIDEBAR, not the feed, so clicking it loads no further posts. Consequence: a live sweep must run at least as often as the busiest tracked author publishes 5 posts, or it will silently under-report rather than error. For Dilger (roughly daily) that means a gap longer than ~5 days loses material. This is the strongest argument for running the social axis WEEKLY at minimum.
(2) REPOSTS SHOW THE ORIGINAL POST'S AGE, not the repost date. A self-repost therefore looks like an old item sitting in a recent feed. Date captures from the original and record the ambiguity; two Osmani captures and one Dudycz capture hit this on 09-04.
(3) RELATIVE AGE STAMPS ('14h', '4d', '1w') ARE DAY-ACCURATE AT BEST. Every capture should say the date came from a relative stamp at a stated retrieval time.
(4) CAPTURE THE CANONICAL PER-POST PERMALINK (linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>/), never the recent-activity feed URL. The feed-URL habit in older raw/notes captures is exactly the weak-citation-chain finding lint raised; all 2026-09-04 captures use permalinks. Read the urn from the post element's own data-urn attribute, and print it alongside the text in the SAME extraction call — pulling text and ids in separate calls caused one misattributed permalink on 09-04 (Miller's urn written onto a Fritzsche post), caught and corrected mid-sweep.
_headless_fetch_constraint: ADDED 2026-09-04, recording the 09-03 run's finding so it stops being rediscovered. web_fetch now enforces a PROVENANCE SET: a URL can only be fetched if it appeared in a user message or in a prior search/fetch result. Blog INDEX pages therefore cannot be polled directly on a headless run — each one needs a WebSearch first purely to mint provenance, which roughly doubles the calls per channel and inserts search ranking (authority, not recency) as an upstream filter on what the watch can even see. The `channels[]` and `blog[]` lists in this file are written as if direct polling works; on a headless run they are SEEDS FOR SEARCH QUERIES, not fetch targets. A scheduled run that reports a channel 'quiet' should say whether it reached the index or only searched for it.

_candidate_primaries_note_2026_09_04: CORRECTION 2026-09-04 after the harness-paper ingest. This list has treated harness optimisation as a handful of named candidate papers to hunt down. That framing is WRONG and the ingest settled it: harness optimisation is a research FIELD with a corpus, not three papers. Evidence: TWO independent surveys exist two months apart with disjoint author sets (Guo et al. arXiv:2606.20683, 17 authors, CityU HK/Sydney/Peking; Ning et al. arXiv:2605.18747, 42 authors, UIUC/Meta/Stanford) — and note Ning et al. is ITSELF A SURVEY, which this config previously assumed was a method paper. There is a shared decomposition vocabulary recurring across groups with no common authors in three countries, method plurality on one problem (AHE observability-driven, HarnessX algebraic composition, HarnessForge harness-policy co-evolution, SBCO verifier-grounded), a shared benchmark culture (Terminal-Bench 2/2.1, SWE-bench Verified, GAIA), and — decisively — internal methodological policing: Wang et al. (2607.12227v2) argue the whole harness-evolution line's reported gains may be search budget and benchmark overfitting rather than better harnesses. Fields, unlike isolated papers, argue about their own measurement. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WATCH: stop hunting named paper ids and start tracking the field. Poll Guo et al.'s standing 'Awesome-Agent-Engineering' bibliography as a CHANNEL, and treat new arXiv harness/loop preprints as a recurring axis rather than one-off candidates. Two already known and uncaptured: arXiv:2603.25723 'Natural-Language Agent Harnesses' and arXiv:2607.21557 'OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment'. STANDING CAVEAT: every paper in this corpus is an un-reviewed preprint, INCLUDING the critique.
